title: Find the Losers of the Circular Game
summary: In a circular game with n friends, the ball is passed starting from the first friend, moving k steps clockwise on the first turn, 2k steps on the second turn, and so on.
statement: In a circular game with n friends, the ball is passed starting from the first friend, moving k steps clockwise on the first turn, 2k steps on the second turn, and so on. The game continues until a friend receives the ball for the second time. The losers are the friends who do not receive the ball at all. Given n and k, return the IDs of the losers in ascending order.
constraints: Friends are numbered one through n, and friend one initially holds the ball.
On turn t starting at one, pass t*k positions clockwise; stop before a friend would receive the ball a second time.
Return never-receiving friend IDs in ascending order.
hints: Track visited zero-based positions in a set.
Start at position zero and mark it before computing the next pass.
Advance by turn*k modulo n and increment the turn until the next position is already visited.
The simulation follows every rule transition exactly; complementing visited positions and converting to one-based IDs yields precisely the sorted losers.
editorial: The simulation follows every rule transition exactly; complementing visited positions and converting to one-based IDs yields precisely the sorted losers.

tests.explanation: Friends one, three, and two receive the ball before repetition, leaving four and five.
The first pass returns immediately to friend one, so friends two, three, and four lose.
